newsitem.title: RWANDA: Heavy fighting around Zairean city of Goma.
newsitem.headline: Heavy fighting around Zairean city of Goma.

text.p: Tutsi fighters and Zairean forces exchanged mortar and machinegun fire on the edge of the eastern Zairean city of Goma on Thursday, sending thousands of refugees fleeing, aid workers and witnesses said.

"We have been seeing heavy fighting since 2.30 a.m. (00:30 GMT) with firing within Goma itself and outgoing and incoming mortar and heavy weapons fire about two km (one mile) north of Goma," said Reuters correspondent Christian Jennings.
He said mortar bombs exploded deep in Goma city in an area two km (one mile) from the neighbouring Rwandan border town of Gisenyi and thousands of refugees were leaving towards the border.

"There is fire from the Zairean army going north from the airport. We spoke this morning with a Zairean military official who said the rebels have broken through a line at Manigi, 10 km (six miles) outside of Goma," said Steve Pratt, an official with the CARE International agency in Goma, speaking by radio.
"The Zairean military official told us we should not worry because the Zaireans would leave the airport and let it be occupied by the other side," he added.

The airport is about four km (2.5 miles) north of the city centre and a key target because aid agencies use it to bring in staff and supplies for refugees and the Zairean military has been bringing in army reinforcements in recent days through it.
"Machinegun and rifle fire turned in the last three hours into mortars," said Michelle Quintaglie, spokeswoman for the World Food Programme in Goma. "The situation has deteriorated very rapidly."

"We are getting reports refugees in Kahindo camp, which is north of Goma and has 115,000 residents, are packing up and are on the move," said Quintaglie, adding Zaireans and Rwandan refugees fled towards Mugunga camp to the west of the city.
Reuters Television Cameraman Hannington Osodo who visited Umbano camp for Zairean Tutsis inside Rwanda but close to the border said he saw thousands of refugees moving out.

Shelling and shooting in Kibumba camp north of Goma on Friday and Saturday prompted 200,000 refugees to flee to Mugunga, swelling its population to some 400,000 and making it the largest refugee camp in the world .

Aid agencies are scrambling to prevent large loss of life from disease and hunger in Mugunga. The U.N. refugee agency says that it has no access to up to 400,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees around Goma and 300,000 more around Goma and Butare town.
